latin: Vides ut alta stet nive candidum
english: Do you see how, with deep snow, stands gleaming white
note: Question runs to line 4. candidum (line 1) agrees with Soracte (line 2): Soracte stands white with deep snow.

english: Soracte, and no longer can they sustain the burden,
note: nec iam sustineant: subjunctive in the indirect question 'how ... no longer'; subject silvae in line 3.

english: the labouring woods, and with frost
the rivers have come to a standstill, sharp?
note: acuto agrees with gelu (line 3): 'with sharp frost'. constiterint: perfect subjunctive, the rivers have stopped (frozen).

english: dissolve the cold, logs upon the hearth
note: dissolve frigus: 'melt away the cold'.

english: generously piling on, and more kindly
draw out the four-year-old, from the Sabine,
note: quadrimum agrees with merum (line 8); Sabina agrees with diota (line 8): 'from the Sabine two-eared jar'.

english: O Thaliarchus, unmixed wine, two-eared jar.
note: Thaliarche: vocative of Thaliarchus. diota: ablative, 'from the two-handled jar' (a Greek word).

english: leave to the gods the rest; who, as soon as
note: simul = simul ac, 'as soon as'.

english: have laid low the winds, on the seething sea
note: stravere: perfect (straverunt).

english: battling it out, neither the cypresses
note: deproeliantis: accusative plural, agrees with ventos (line 10).

english: nor the old ash-trees are shaken.

latin: quid sit futurum cras, fuge quaerere et
english: what is going to be tomorrow, flee from asking, and
note: fuge quaerere: 'flee to ask', i.e. avoid asking.

latin: quem Fors dierum cumque dabit, lucro
english: whatever of days Chance will give, to profit
note: quem ... cumque: tmesis of quemcumque, 'whichever (day)'. Fors: Chance personified.

english: set it down, and not sweet loves
note: lucro adpone: 'set down to profit', count as gain. nec negates sperne (line 16).

english: spurn, a boy, nor you the dances,
note: puer: 'being a boy', while you are a boy. neque tu (sperne) choreas: 'nor you spurn the dances'.

english: while from the green one white hair is absent,
note: virenti: dative, 'from you (who are) green', i.e. in your fresh youth.

latin: morosa. nunc et campus et areae
english: peevish. Now both the Campus and the squares
note: morosa agrees with canities (line 17). campus: the Campus Martius. areae: open spaces, courtyards.

english: and soft, towards night, whispers
at the appointed hour let be sought again,
note: repetantur: jussive subjunctive; subjects campus, areae, susurri.

english: now also, of the hiding one, the betrayer, from the inmost
note: latentis agrees with puellae (line 22): 'of the hiding girl'. intumo = intimo.

english: pleasing, of the girl, laughter, from the corner,
note: Construe: the pleasing laughter of the hiding girl, betrayer from the inmost corner.

english: and a pledge snatched from arms
note: lacertis: 'from (her) arms'; the pledge is a bracelet or ring taken from her.

english: or from a finger badly resisting.
note: male pertinaci: 'badly (i.e. scarcely) holding on', a finger that resists only feebly.

english: Mercury, eloquent grandson of Atlas,
note: Mercuri: vocative of Mercurius.

english: who the wild ways of men newly made
note: recentum = recentium: men newly created, primitive.

english: by speech shaped, clever, and of the comely
note: formasti = formavisti. decorae agrees with palaestrae (line 4).

english: by the custom of the wrestling-ground,
note: palaestra: the wrestling school; 'by the custom of the comely wrestling-school'.

latin: te canam, magni Iovis et deorum
english: you I shall sing, of great Jupiter and of the gods
the messenger, and of the curved lyre the parent,
clever, whatever has pleased you, in playful
note: iocoso agrees with furto (line 8): 'in playful theft'. placuit: 'has pleased (you)'.

english: to stow away, theft.
note: callidum ... condere: 'clever at stowing away'; furto: 'by (playful) theft'.

english: you, once, unless you had given back the cattle
note: te is object of risit (line 12): 'laughed at you'. Words of Apollo's threat reported indirectly.

english: by trickery removed, a boy, with threatening
note: amotas agrees with boves (line 9). puerum: you, then a boy. minaci agrees with voce (line 11).

english: voice while he frightens, bereft of his quiver,
note: viduus pharetra: 'widowed of (his) quiver'; Mercury had stolen it as well. 'his' supplied.

english: Apollo laughed.

latin: quin et Atridas duce te superbos
english: indeed also the sons of Atreus, with you as guide, the proud
note: Atridas: the Atridae, Agamemnon and Menelaus. superbos agrees with Atridas.

english: Ilium left behind, rich Priam
note: Ilio relicto: ablative absolute.

english: and the Thessalian fires and, hostile to Troy,
note: iniqua agrees with castra (line 16): 'the camp hostile to Troy'.

english: the camp, eluded.
note: fefellit: 'escaped the notice of'; objects Atridas, ignis, castra.

english: you the pious souls in happy
note: laetis agrees with sedibus (line 18): 'in happy abodes'.

english: abodes lay to rest, and with a wand the light
note: levem agrees with turbam (line 19).

english: golden, the throng; to the upper of the gods
note: aurea agrees with virga (line 18): 'with golden wand'. superis deorum: 'to the gods above'.

english: pleasing, and to the lowest.
note: imis: 'to the lowest (gods)', those below.

latin: Tu ne quaesieris, scire nefas, quem mihi, quem tibi
english: You, do not ask — to know is unlawful — what for me, what for you
note: ne quaesieris: perfect subjunctive prohibition. quem (masculine) agrees with finem (line 2): 'what end for me, what for you'. nefas: forbidden by divine law.

latin: finem di dederint, Leuconoe, nec Babylonios
english: end the gods have given, Leuconoe, and not Babylonian
note: dederint: perfect subjunctive in indirect question.

latin: temptaris numeros. ut melius, quidquid erit, pati.
english: numbers try. How better, whatever will be, to endure!
note: temptaris = temptaveris, prohibition continued by nec. Babylonios numeros: astrological calculations. ut melius: exclamation.

latin: seu pluris hiemes seu tribuit Iuppiter ultimam,
english: whether more winters, or Jupiter has allotted as the last

latin: quae nunc oppositis debilitat pumicibus mare
english: the one which now on opposing pumice-stones weakens the sea
note: quae refers to the winter (hiemem understood with ultimam): the winter which wears out the sea against the rocks.

latin: Tyrrhenum: sapias, vina liques et spatio brevi
english: Tyrrhenian: be wise, strain the wines, and to a brief span
note: sapias, liques, reseces: subjunctives of exhortation. spatio brevi: 'because of the brief span', or 'to (fit) a brief span'.

latin: spem longam reseces. dum loquimur, fugerit invida
english: long hope cut back. While we speak, will have fled grudging
note: reseces: pruning metaphor, 'cut back' (like a vine); meaning: curtail far-reaching hopes. invida agrees with aetas (line 8).

latin: aetas: carpe diem quam minimum credula postero.
english: time: pluck the day, as little as possible trusting the next.
note: carpe diem: 'pluck the day' (metaphor of gathering fruit or flowers): make use of today. credula agrees with Leuconoe. postero: 'to the next (day)'.

latin: Quem virum aut heroa lyra vel acri
english: What man or hero, on the lyre or on the shrill
note: acri agrees with tibia (line 2).

english: pipe, do you take up to celebrate, Clio?
note: Clio: the Muse of history.

english: what god? whose will re-echo, playful,
note: iocosa agrees with imago (line 4): 'the playful image' will sing back.

english: name the image
note: imago: 'image', here the echo. Construe: whose name will the playful echo sing back.

english: either on the shady of Helicon borders
note: umbrosis agrees with oris: 'on the shady slopes of Helicon'.

latin: aut super Pindo gelidove in Haemo?
english: or upon Pindus, or on cold Haemus?
whence the vocal one, heedlessly having followed,
note: vocalem agrees with Orphea (line 8). insecutae agrees with silvae (line 8).

english: Orpheus, the woods,
note: Construe: whence (from Haemus) the woods followed tuneful Orpheus heedlessly.

english: by maternal art the swift delaying
note: arte materna: art from his mother, the Muse Calliope. rapidos agrees with lapsus (line 10). morantem agrees with Orphea.

english: glidings of rivers and the swift winds,
charming too the eared, with tuneful strings,
note: blandum: '(so) charming (as) to lead'. auritas agrees with quercus (line 12): oaks given ears. fidibus canoris: 'with tuneful strings'.

english: to lead, oaks.
What shall I say before the customary of the Parent
note: solitis agrees with laudibus (line 14): 'before the customary praises of the Parent' (Jupiter).

latin: laudibus, qui res hominum ac deorum,
english: praises, who the affairs of men and of gods,

latin: qui mare ac terras variisque mundum
english: who the sea and the lands and, with varied, the universe
note: variis agrees with horis (line 16).

english: governs, seasons?
note: temperat: 'regulates'. horis: 'with (varied) seasons'.

english: whence nothing greater is begotten than himself
note: ipso: ablative of comparison.

latin: nec viget quidquam simile aut secundum.
english: nor flourishes anything like or second.
the nearest to him, however, has seized
note: proximos agrees with honores (line 20).

english: Pallas, the honours,
in battles bold. Nor you shall I pass over in silence,
note: audax agrees with Pallas, as the source punctuates (stop after audax); some editors attach proeliis audax to Liber in line 22.

english: Liber, and, to savage hostile, maiden
note: Liber: Bacchus. inimica agrees with virgo: the maiden (Diana) hostile to savage beasts.

english: beasts, nor you, to be feared for the sure
note: metuende: vocative gerundive, 'you who are to be feared'. certa agrees with sagitta (line 24).

english: Phoebus, arrow.
note: certa sagitta: 'for (your) unerring arrow'.

english: I shall tell also of Alcides and the boys of Leda,
note: Alciden: Alcides, Hercules. pueros Ledae: Castor and Pollux.

english: this one with horses, that one at overcoming with fists
note: superare: infinitive with nobilem (line 27): 'famous for overcoming'.

english: famous; whose, as soon as, white to sailors,
note: quorum ... alba ... stella: 'whose white star'. simul = as soon as.

english: star has shone back,
note: refulsit: the star of the Dioscuri, St Elmo's fire, seen by sailors.

english: flows down from the rocks the stirred-up spray,
note: umor: 'moisture', the spray. Order: the stirred-up water flows down from the rocks.

english: the winds fall, and the clouds flee,

latin: et minax, quia sic voluere, ponto
english: and the threatening, because thus they willed, on the sea
note: minax agrees with unda (line 32). voluere: perfect (voluerunt), 'they' = the Dioscuri.

english: wave lies back down.

latin: Romulum post hos prius an quietum
english: Romulus after these first, or the quiet
note: Indirect questions depending on dubito (line 35): whether I should recall first Romulus or ...

english: reign of Pompilius shall I recall, or the proud
note: Pompili: Numa Pompilius. memorem: deliberative subjunctive.

english: rods of Tarquinius, I am in doubt, or of Cato
note: fascis: the fasces, rods of office; Tarquinius Superbus. Catonis: Cato of Utica.

english: the noble death:
Regulus and the Scauri and of his great soul
note: animae magnae prodigum: 'lavish of his great soul' (life). 'his' supplied.

english: prodigal Paulus, the Carthaginian prevailing,
note: superante Poeno: ablative absolute, at Cannae. Poeno: 'the Phoenician', Carthaginian (Hannibal).

english: grateful, with distinguished, I shall record, Camena,
note: insigni agrees with camena: 'with a distinguished Camena', i.e. in noble verse. Camena: Italian Muse.

english: and Fabricius.
him and, with unkempt, Curius, hair,
note: incomptis agrees with capillis: 'Curius with unkempt hair'.

english: useful in war, bore, and Camillus,
harsh poverty and an ancestral, with fitting
note: avitus agrees with fundus (line 44); apto agrees with lare.

english: with household god, farm.
note: apto cum lare: 'with a household (god) fitted to it', a homestead matching the farm. lar: the household god, metonymy for home.

english: grows, by hidden, like a tree, time
note: occulto agrees with aevo: 'in unseen lapse of time'.

english: the fame of Marcellus; gleams among all
note: Marcelli: of Marcellus (the conqueror of Syracuse, with allusion to the young Marcellus). Text doubtful: some editors emend to Marcellis (dative); source reading kept.

english: the Julian star, as among fires
note: Iulium sidus: the star of the Julian house (Caesar's comet). ignis: accusative plural.

english: the moon the lesser.
note: minores agrees with ignis (line 47): 'among the lesser fires'.

english: of the human race father and guardian,
sprung from Saturn, to you the care of great
note: orte Saturno: vocative participle, to Jupiter, son of Saturn.

english: Caesar by the fates has been given: you, with second
note: secundo Caesare: ablative absolute, 'with Caesar (as) second'.

english: Caesar, may you reign.
note: regnes: jussive or optative subjunctive.

english: he, whether the Parthians, over Latium looming,
note: imminentis: accusative plural agreeing with Parthos.

english: shall have driven, tamed, in a just triumph,
or, lying under the shores of the East,
note: subiectos agrees with Seras et Indos (line 56): those who lie under (bordering) the regions of the Orient. orae: dative.

english: the Seres and the Indians,
note: Seras: the Seres, the Chinese.

latin: te minor latum reget aequos orbem:
english: lesser than you, the broad will rule, just, world:
note: te minor: 'inferior to you'. latum agrees with orbem. aequos = aequus, nominative: he as a just ruler.

english: you with heavy chariot will shake Olympus,
you, on too-little chaste, hostile, will send
note: parum castis agrees with lucis (line 60): 'on unchaste groves'. inimica agrees with fulmina.

english: thunderbolts, groves.
note: fulmina inimica: 'hostile thunderbolts'. lucis: dative, 'onto the groves' (profaned groves).

english: When you, Lydia, Telephus's
note: Telephi: genitive of Telephus, with cervicem (line 2).

english: neck rosy, the waxen of Telephus
note: cerea agrees with bracchia (line 3): 'the waxen arms of Telephus'.

english: you praise, arms, alas, my
seething with difficult bile swells liver.
note: meum ... iecur: 'my liver' swells. difficili bile: 'with peevish bile'; the liver as seat of anger and passion.

latin: tum nec mens mihi nec color
english: then neither mind for me nor colour

latin: certa sede manet, umor et in genas
english: in fixed seat remains, and moisture onto the cheeks
note: certa sede: 'in a sure place'. umor: a tear.

english: stealthily glides, proving
note: arguens: 'proving', showing.

english: how by slow, deep within, I am steeped, fires.
note: lentis agrees with ignibus: 'with slow fires'. macerer: 'I am soaked, wasted'; metaphor of steeping, meaning consumed.

english: I burn, whether for you the white
have fouled shoulders, immoderate in unmixed wine,
note: turparunt = turpaverunt. inmodicae agrees with rixae (line 11). mero: 'with unmixed wine'.

english: brawls, or a boy raging
has pressed a remembering, with his tooth, on the lips, mark.
note: memorem agrees with notam: 'a mark that remembers', a lasting mark. 'his' supplied; labris: 'on (your) lips'.

english: Not, if me enough you were to hear,
note: non goes with speres (line 14): 'you would not hope'.

english: would you hope lasting, the sweet barbarously
note: perpetuum: '(him) lasting', Telephus as constant; 'him' understood. dulcia agrees with oscula (line 15).

english: harming, kisses, which Venus
note: laedentem agrees with the understood 'him': 'one who barbarously hurts the sweet kisses'.

english: with the fifth part of her nectar has steeped.
note: quinta parte: the quintessence, the finest part. sui: 'of her own' nectar.

english: happy thrice and more

latin: quos inrupta tenet copula nec malis
english: whom an unbroken holds bond, and not by bad
note: inrupta agrees with copula: 'an unbroken bond'. nec negates solvet (line 20). malis agrees with querimoniis (line 19).

english: torn apart, complaints,
note: divolsus agrees with amor (line 20): 'love torn apart by bad complaints'.

english: sooner than the last will love release, day.
note: suprema ... die: 'than the last day'. solvet: 'will release (them)'.

latin: O navis, referent in mare te novi
english: O ship, will carry back to sea you new
note: novi agrees with fluctus (line 2). The ship is commonly read as an allegory of the state.

latin: fluctus. o quid agis? fortiter occupa
english: waves. Oh, what are you doing? Bravely seize
the harbour. Do you not see how
bare of oarage the side
note: nudum agrees with latus: 'the side bare of oars'; the verb is supplied from gemant (line 6).

english: and the mast, by swift wounded Africus,
note: celeri agrees with Africo: 'wounded by the swift Africus' (the south-west wind).

english: and the yards groan, and without ropes
note: gemant: subjunctive in indirect question after vides ut. funibus: undergirding cables.

english: scarcely to endure the keels
are able the more imperious
note: imperiosius agrees with aequor (line 9): 'the too imperious sea'. carinae: plural for the hull.

latin: aequor? non tibi sunt integra lintea,
english: sea? Not for you are whole sails,
note: lintea: 'linen', sails.

latin: non di, quos iterum pressa voces malo.
english: not gods, whom again, pressed, you might call on, by evil.
note: di: images of the gods on the stern, lost. pressa agrees with the ship: 'pressed by evil'. voces: subjunctive.

english: although, Pontic pine,
note: Pontica pinus: vocative, the ship built of Pontic pine.

english: of a forest the daughter noble,

latin: iactes et genus et nomen inutile:
english: you boast both lineage and name useless:
nothing, in painted, the timid sailor, sterns
note: nil ... fidit: 'trusts not at all'. pictis agrees with puppibus: 'in painted sterns'.

english: trusts. You, unless to the winds
note: nisi ... debes ludibrium: 'unless you owe the winds a mockery'.

english: you owe a plaything, beware.
note: ludibrium: 'a plaything, mockery'; meaning: unless you are fated to be the sport of the winds.

english: lately anxious which to me weariness,
note: quae: 'you who'. sollicitum taedium: 'an anxious weariness', a cause of disgust. mihi: 'to me'.

english: now longing and care not light,
poured between the shining
note: interfusa agrees with aequora (line 20): seas poured between. nitentis agrees with Cycladas.

english: may you avoid seas, Cyclades.
note: vites: subjunctive of wish. Cycladas: accusative, Greek form; the Cyclades islands.

latin: Pastor cum traheret per freta navibus
english: When the shepherd was dragging across the straits in ships
note: Pastor: Paris, the shepherd of Ida.

english: Idaean Helen, the faithless one, his hostess,
note: Idaeis agrees with navibus: 'Idaean ships' (built of timber from Ida). perfidus agrees with pastor. hospitam: Helen, wife of his host. 'his' supplied.

english: in unwelcome the swift overwhelmed calm
note: ingrato agrees with otio: 'in an unwelcome calm'. celeres agrees with ventos (line 4). Subject: Nereus (line 5).

english: winds, that he might sing the fierce
Nereus fates. "With evil you lead omen home
note: fera agrees with fata. mala ... avi: 'with an evil bird', bad omen. Quotation marks as in the source: Nereus' prophecy begins here and runs to the end of the poem.

english: whom with much will seek again Greece soldiery
note: quam: Helen (feminine). multo agrees with milite: 'with many a soldier' (collective singular); Graecia is subject.

english: sworn together to break your nuptials
note: coniurata agrees with Graecia.

english: and the kingdom of Priam old.

latin: heu heu, quantus equis, quantus adest viris
english: alas, alas, how much for horses, how much is at hand for men
note: quantus agrees with sudor (line 10).

english: sweat, how many you set in motion funerals for the Dardanian
note: Dardanae agrees with genti (line 11).

latin: genti. iam galeam Pallas et aegida
english: race. Already the helmet Pallas and the aegis
note: aegida: Greek accusative of aegis, Pallas' shield.

english: and the chariot and the rage prepares.
In vain, on Venus' protection fierce,
you will comb your hair and, pleasing to women,
note: caesariem: 'the long hair'. 'your' supplied. grata agrees with carmina (line 15).

english: on the unwarlike lyre songs you will divide;
note: divides: 'you will apportion', sing in parts, measures.

english: in vain in the bedchamber the heavy
note: gravis agrees with hastas (line 17).

english: spears and of the reed the points Cnosian
note: calami spicula: 'the points of the reed', arrows. Cnosii agrees with calami: Cretan (Cnossian) reed.

english: you will avoid, and the din, and swift to pursue
note: celerem sequi: 'swift to pursue', with Aiacem.

english: Ajax: nevertheless, alas, late, adulterous
note: serus: 'late', though late. adulteros agrees with crines (line 20).

english: hair with dust you will defile.
note: collines: 'you will smear'; dust of death.

english: Not the son of Laertes, ruin of your
note: Laertiaden: Ulysses.

english: race, not Pylian Nestor, do you look back at?
note: respicis: 'do you regard', see behind you.

english: press, fearless, you, Salaminian
note: urgent: subjects Teucer, Sthenelus. inpavidi: nominative plural.

english: Teucer, you Sthenelus, skilled
note: sciens: 'knowing', skilled, with pugnae (line 25).

latin: pugnae sive opus est imperitare equis,
english: of fight, or, if there is need to command horses,
note: sive: 'or, if' (sive ... opus est).

english: no charioteer sluggish. Meriones also
note: non auriga piger: 'not a sluggish charioteer'.

latin: nosces. ecce furit, te reperire atrox,
english: you will come to know. Look, he rages to find you, fierce,
note: te reperire: 'to find you'. atrox agrees with Tydides.

english: the son of Tydeus, better than his father:
note: Tydides: Diomedes. 'his' supplied.

latin: quem tu, cervus uti vallis in altera
english: whom you, as a stag, of a valley in the other
note: uti = ut. altera agrees with parte (line 30): 'in the other part of the valley'.

english: seen part, a wolf, of the grass unmindful,
note: visum agrees with lupum: 'a wolf seen'. inmemor: 'forgetful of the grass' (the stag).

english: with high you will flee, soft, panting,
note: sublimi anhelitu: 'with high (deep, upheaved) panting'. mollis: 'soft one', effeminate.

english: not this having promised your.
note: tuae: 'to your (woman)', Helen. pollicitus: 'having promised'.

english: the angry will postpone the day for Ilium
note: iracunda agrees with classis (line 34): 'the wrathful fleet'.

english: and for the matrons of the Phrygians, fleet of Achilles;
note: Achillei: genitive of Achilles.

english: after fixed winters will burn Achaean
note: certas hiemes: 'a fixed number of winters'. Achaicus agrees with ignis (line 36).

english: fire Ilian houses.
note: Closing quotation mark absent in source; Nereus' speech ends here.

english: O daughter more beautiful than a beautiful mother,
note: matre pulcra: ablative of comparison.

english: whatever for accusing you will wish, limit
note: quem ... cumque: tmesis of quemcumque, agreeing with modum: 'whatever end'. criminosis agrees with iambis (line 3): 'abusive iambics'.

english: you will put on iambics, whether with flame
note: pones: 'you will set (an end) to'. iambis: dative.

english: or with sea it pleases, Hadriatic.
note: mari Hadriano: 'in the Adriatic sea'.

english: not Dindymene, not in the sanctuaries shakes
note: Dindymene: Cybele of Mount Dindymus. adytis: 'in the inner shrines'. Negatives govern quatit.

english: the mind of priests the dweller Pythian,
note: incola Pythius: Apollo, dweller of Pytho (Delphi).

english: not Liber equally, not the sharp
note: acuta agrees with aera (line 8): 'the shrill bronzes' (cymbals).

english: so redouble Corybantes bronzes,
note: geminant: 'double', clash together. sic ... ut: 'so ... as'.

latin: tristes ut irae, quas neque Noricus
english: as grim angers, which neither Norican
note: tristes agrees with irae. Noricus agrees with ensis (line 10): sword of Noric steel.

english: deters sword nor sea shipwrecking
note: naufragum: 'shipwrecking'.

english: nor savage fire nor, with tremendous,
note: saevos = saevus. tremendo agrees with tumultu (line 12).

english: Jupiter himself rushing down, tumult.
is said Prometheus, to add to the original
note: fertur: 'is said'. principi agrees with limo (line 14): 'to the primal clay'.

english: clay compelled, a particle from everywhere
note: coactus: 'forced'. particulam: 'a small portion' from every creature.

english: cut off, and of the mad lion
note: desectam agrees with particulam.

english: the violence to the stomach to have applied our.
note: nostro agrees with stomacho: 'to our stomach', the seat of anger.

english: angers Thyestes with ruin heavy
note: irae: subject. gravi agrees with exitio.

english: laid low, and for lofty cities the final
note: stravere: perfect (straverunt). ultimae agrees with causae (line 19).

english: have stood causes, why they should perish
note: stetere: perfect (steterunt), 'have stood (as)', been.

english: utterly, and should press on walls
a hostile plough an army insolent.
note: The victor ploughed over the site of the destroyed city.

english: restrain your mind: me also of the breast
note: mentem: 'mind', here passion. 'your' supplied.

english: tested in sweet youth
note: temptavit: 'tried', assailed.

english: the fever, and into swift iambics
note: fervor: 'heat, ferment' of the breast.

english: sent raging. Now I, with mild
note: mitibus: 'with mild things', gentler verses. furentem agrees with me (line 22).

english: to exchange seek the grim, provided that to me
note: tristia: 'the bitter things'. dum: 'provided that'.

english: you become, recanted, a friend
note: recantatis agrees with opprobriis (line 28): 'the reproaches being recanted' (ablative absolute).

english: reproaches, and your heart give back.
note: animum reddas: 'give back (your) heart'. 'your' supplied.
